label: Train-only interpretation of the frozen candidates (descriptive; feeds no selection and changes no frozen choice). Produced by `fremtpl2 interpret`.

notes.exposure_offset: The frequency GBM was trained with log(Exposure) as init_score. The exposure offset is outside the contributions: the contributions (and the base value) explain the raw score, the log of the ANNUAL claim rate; the expected count is exp(raw score + log Exposure). The severity GBM has no offset; the Tweedie GBM uses Exposure only as a weight.
notes.contributions: A contribution is the TreeSHAP attribution of one row's raw (log-scale) score to one feature, relative to the base value of the model. It describes that model on that row; it is not a coefficient and individual contributions are never equated with GLM coefficients. Group means of contributions are compared with GLM log relativities only on the aligned log scale after re-centring on the GLM reference level, and the GBM mean contribution of a level also carries the part of the effect that the model shares with correlated factors and interactions.

glm_comparison.label: mean GBM contribution per GLM level, re-centred on the GLM reference level, against the log GLM relativity exp(beta) of the stored coefficients of the GLM of the SELECTED GLM candidate for the same component (results/glm_models.json, on its own feature map and reference levels; a factor the GLM does not contain is absent, effect 0), plus any other stored GLM of the same target as a labelled extra column (aligned log scale; not coefficients)

interaction.label: exploratory and descriptive, train sample only; no GLM interaction is refitted (deferred by the 2026-11-08 amendment); the DrivAge contribution varies with VehPower only through the interactions the trees learned, shared with the VehPower contribution

monotonicity.label: pure premium of each candidate along a BonusMalus sweep, all other features fixed at the row's own values; a decrease is a relative step below -tolerance between consecutive points; the sweep points are the distinct train BonusMalus values or, if there are more than max_points, an equally spaced grid from the train minimum to the train maximum (so a decrease between two consecutive points of the grid is not seen); the rows swept are a fixed train sub-sample; a diagnostic on train rows that feeds no selection

bonus_malus_only.constraint: frequency: GLM (log-linear in BonusMalus); severity: constant

glm_freq_x_sev[simplified].constraint: frequency: GLM (log-linear in BonusMalus); severity: GLM (log-linear in BonusMalus)

gbm_freq_x_sev.constraint: frequency: GBM constrained; severity: GBM unconstrained

monotonicity.statement: Only the frequency and the Tweedie GBM are constrained to be non-decreasing in BonusMalus. The GBM frequency x severity pure premium is a product with the unconstrained severity GBM and is not guaranteed to be monotone; a decrease is reported as a limit, never retuned.

constraint_register.rationale: A worse claims record (higher BonusMalus) should not lower the expected claim frequency or pure premium: the constraint removes non-monotone artefacts of a tree ensemble on this factor. It is frozen in protocol section 5 (frequency Poisson and Tweedie GBMs non-decreasing in BonusMalus; severity Gamma GBM and all other factors unconstrained).

implementation.how: LightGBM monotone_constraints on the BonusMalus column (1 = non-decreasing), fixed in config models.gbm.components.*.monotone

verification.note: the raw-score sweep of the constrained components must not decrease (minimum step >= -tolerance); the severity GBM is unconstrained and listed for comparison; the pure premium sweep is in the monotonicity block

cv_effect.label: CV-only diagnostic of the frozen monotone constraint; never a candidate and never an input of any selection
cv_effect.scores_label: GBM CV scores are optimistic tuning scores: early stopping and grid scoring use the same registered fold (protocol section 5)
cv_effect.sign: differences are unconstrained minus constrained: a negative value means the unconstrained variant has the lower (better) loss
cv_effect.separately_tuned_note: comparison of two separately tuned procedures (identical grid, folds, seed and budget), so the hyperparameters and rounds differ between the variants
cv_effect.controlled_ablation_note: same chosen hyperparameters and rounds, the constraint toggled
cv_effect.kind: optimistic tuning scores of CV folds also used for early stopping and grid scoring; not unbiased estimates and not test results

constraint_register.grid_edge_disclosure: The hyperparameter grid was committed before tuning and was not extended after seeing the CV results. The grid axes have 2 values; 9 of the 9 chosen values lie on the lowest or highest value of their axis, so the optimum may lie outside the grid along those axes (with two values per axis every chosen value is on the boundary); the chosen points are not claimed to be the most complex or the simplest model of the grid.
